verses.text: Again Jesus began to teach by the lake. The crowd around him was so large that he got into a boat on the lake and sat down. All the people stayed on the shore.
He taught them many things by using stories. In his teaching he said,
"Listen! A farmer went out to plant his seed.
As he was scattering the seed, some fell on the path, and the birds came and ate it up.
Some fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil. It grew up quickly, because the soil was not deep.
But when the sun came up, the plants dried up. They withered because they had no roots.
Some seed fell among thorns. The thorns grew up and choked the plants, so they did not produce any grain.
But some seed fell on good soil. It grew up and produced a crop. Some plants produced thirty times more than was planted, some sixty times and some a hundred times."
Then Jesus said, "Whoever has ears should listen."
Later, when Jesus was alone, the twelve and the others around him asked him about the stories.
He told them, "You have been given the secret of the kingdom of God. But to people outside, everything is said in stories.
This is so that, 'They will look and look, but never see. They will listen and listen, but never understand. If they did, they might turn to God and be forgiven.'"
Then Jesus said to them, "Do you not understand this story? Then how will you understand any of the stories?
The farmer plants God's message.
Some people are like the seed on the path, where the message is planted. As soon as they hear it, Satan comes and takes away the message that was planted in them.
Others are like the seed planted on rocky ground. They hear the message and straight away accept it with joy.
But they have no roots, so they last only a short time. When trouble or hard times come because of the message, they quickly give up.
Others are like the seed planted among thorns. They hear the message,
but the worries of this life, the false promise of riches and the wish for other things come in and choke the message. So it produces no fruit.
Others are like the seed planted on good soil. They hear the message, accept it and produce a crop. Some produce thirty times more than was planted, some sixty times and some a hundred times."
Jesus said to them, "Do you bring in a lamp to put it under a bowl or under a bed? No, you put it on a stand.
Whatever is hidden is meant to be shown. Whatever is secret is meant to be brought out into the open.
Whoever has ears should listen."
He went on, "Think carefully about what you hear. The same amount you give to others will be given back to you, and even more.
Whoever has something will be given more. But whoever does not have anything, even what they have will be taken away from them."
Jesus also said, "The kingdom of God is like a man who scatters seed on the ground.
Night and day, while he sleeps and while he is awake, the seed comes up and grows. But he does not know how it happens.
The soil makes the grain grow all by itself. First the stalk comes up, then the head, and then the full grain in the head.
As soon as the grain is ripe, he cuts it with his sickle, because the time to harvest has come."
Jesus said again, "What can we say the kingdom of God is like? What story can we use to explain it?
It is like a mustard seed, which is the smallest of all the seeds planted in the ground.
But when it is planted, it grows and becomes the largest of all garden plants. It grows such big branches that the birds can rest in its shade."
Jesus used many stories like these to teach the people God's message, as much as they could understand.
He did not say anything to them without using a story. But when he was alone with his own followers, he explained everything to them.
That day, when evening came, Jesus said to his followers, "Let us go over to the other side of the lake."
They left the crowd behind and took Jesus along in the boat he was already in. There were also other boats with him.
A very strong wind came up. The waves crashed over the boat, so that it was nearly filled with water.
Jesus was in the back of the boat, sleeping on a cushion. The followers woke him up and said, "Teacher, do you not care if we drown?"
Jesus got up and gave orders to the wind. He said to the waves, "Quiet! Be still!" Then the wind stopped, and it was completely calm.
He said to his followers, "Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?"
They were terrified and asked each other, "Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!"
